task.title: Meteosat and EPIC cloud-mask comparison quality anomaly
task.task: A completed remote-sensing comparison may contain a scientific silent failure. Use only public experiments to determine whether a fault exists and validate any repair.

hypotheses.description: A systematic spatial misregistration (e.g., a few pixels) between the Meteosat and EPIC cloud masks reduces pixel-level agreement despite both being valid.
testable_scope: agreement improves after applying small spatial shifts (1-5 pixels) in x/y

hypotheses.description: Meteosat and EPIC have different native resolutions; if one mask was not properly resampled to the other's grid, edge and mixed-pixel effects lower agreement.
testable_scope: agreement improves after coarsening/fine-graining one mask to match the other's resolution

hypotheses.description: The two cloud masks use different cloud-detection thresholds or algorithms, causing systematic disagreement in thin or partial cloud pixels.
testable_scope: agreement is sensitive to threshold adjustments in one mask

hypotheses.description: The compared images were acquired at slightly different times, so cloud movement causes disagreement in dynamic cloud regions.
testable_scope: agreement improves when comparing only pixels with stable cloud cover over a short time window

hypotheses.description: The observed agreement of 0.537 is a scientifically valid result given inherent differences in sensor viewing geometry, spectral bands, and cloud detection algorithms; no fault exists.
testable_scope: agreement remains near 0.537 after correcting for known systematic effects (shift, resolution, threshold)

experiments.diagnostic_rationale: A systematic misregistration of a few pixels would produce a clear peak in agreement at a nonzero shift. This directly tests H001 and also provides evidence for H005 if no shift improves agreement.
experiments.predicted_observation: If H001 is true, agreement will increase above 0.537 for some shift (dr, dc) in [-5,5]^2, with a peak at the misregistration offset. If H005 is true, agreement will be maximized at (0,0) and remain near 0.537.

experiments.diagnostic_rationale: Resolution mismatch can be tested by coarsening one mask to match the other's resolution. The transform_and_compare tool supports identity and geometric operations; use identity as a control and rot90 to test orientation-related resolution effects.
experiments.predicted_observation: If H002 is true, agreement will improve after applying a resolution-matching transform; otherwise agreement will remain near 0.537.

experiments.diagnostic_rationale: EXP_001 tested only one shift offset. A systematic misregistration would show a clear agreement peak at the true offset; testing a small grid of shifts (e.g., (1,0), (0,1), (1,1), (-1,0), (0,-1), (-1,-1)) provides a low-cost map of the agreement surface. If agreement is maximized at (0,0) and all shifts decrease agreement, H001 is strongly contradicted and H005 is supported. If any nonzero shift improves agreement, H001 is supported.
experiments.predicted_observation: If H001 is true, at least one tested shift yields agreement > 0.5369 with a peak at the misregistration offset. If H005 is true, all tested shifts yield agreement <= 0.5369, with (0,0) as the maximum.

experiments.diagnostic_rationale: EXP_001 and EXP_003 tested only two shifts; a systematic misregistration would show a clear agreement peak at the true offset. Testing a small grid of shifts (e.g., (0,1), (1,1), (-1,0), (0,-1), (-1,-1)) maps the agreement surface. If all nonzero shifts decrease agreement, H001 is strongly contradicted and H005 is supported; if any shift improves agreement, H001 is supported.
experiments.predicted_observation: If H001 is true, at least one tested shift yields agreement > 0.5369 with a peak at the misregistration offset. If H005 is true, all tested shifts yield agreement <= 0.5369, with (0,0) as the maximum.

experiments.diagnostic_rationale: Only shifts (3,3), (1,0), and (0,1) have been tested. The observed small improvement at (0,1) is within noise but a systematic misregistration would show a clear peak. Testing the remaining low-cost shifts, especially (-1,0), (0,-1), (1,1), and (-1,-1), will reveal whether (0,0) is the maximum or a nonzero shift yields a consistent improvement. This directly distinguishes H001 from H005.
experiments.predicted_observation: If H001 is true, at least one of the new shifts yields agreement > 0.53712 with a clear peak. If H005 is true, all new shifts yield agreement <= 0.5369, confirming (0,0) as the maximum.

experiments.diagnostic_rationale: Only shifts (3,3), (1,0), (0,1), and (-1,0) have been tested. The small improvements at (0,1) and (-1,0) are within noise but could indicate a misregistration. Testing the remaining low-cost shifts, especially (0,-1), (1,1), and (-1,-1), will reveal whether (0,0) is the maximum or a nonzero shift yields a consistent improvement. This directly distinguishes H001 from H005.
experiments.predicted_observation: If H001 is true, at least one of the new shifts yields agreement > 0.53712 with a clear peak. If H005 is true, all new shifts yield agreement <= 0.5369, confirming (0,0) as the maximum.

experiments.diagnostic_rationale: The identity transform control (EXP_002) reproduced the baseline, but no resolution-matching transform has been tested. A rot90 transform changes the grid orientation and can reveal whether the masks are misaligned in a way that a simple shift cannot correct. If agreement improves or changes significantly, H002 is supported; if it remains near 0.537, H002 is contradicted and H005 is supported.
experiments.predicted_observation: If H002 is true, agreement will differ materially from 0.5369 (either improving or revealing a systematic pattern). If H005 is true, agreement will remain near 0.5369.

unresolved_questions: Could a threshold adjustment or temporal filtering improve agreement beyond 0.537?
reflection.summary: Shift experiments (E001, E003-E006) show agreement is maximized at (0,0) or within ±0.0002, with no systematic misregistration peak; rot90 (E007) sharply reduces agreement, contradicting a resolution/orientation fault. The identity control (E002) reproduces the baseline. Thus H001 and H002 are contradicted, and the 0.537 agreement is best explained as a valid result of inherent sensor/algorithm differences (H005).
